output_json.patch_notes: In Expand.extractFile(), immediately after `File f = FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName);`, added a containment guard: compute `dir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator` and `f.getCanonicalPath()`, and throw an Exception ("Entry is outside of the target directory: ...") unless the resolved canonical path is the destination directory itself or lies beneath it. This blocks all four reported sink paths (write at line 178, mkdirs at 169, parent mkdirs at 165, setLastModified at 204) since the check runs before any of them. Added ExpandTest with two JUnit-3-style cases matching the existing test structure: testZipSlipEntryIsRejected (a "../escaped.txt" entry is not written outside dest) and testNormalEntryIsExtracted (a normal "sub/good.txt" entry still extracts correctly), ensuring the fix preserves expected behavior.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The guard only rejects entries that canonicalize outside the destination directory; legitimate entries (including nested subdirectories) are unaffected, as verified by testNormalEntryIsExtracted and the full ExpandTest run. The containment check uses canonical-path prefix matching with a trailing File.separator to avoid sibling-prefix false positives (e.g. "/dest" vs "/dest-evil"). Behavior on a malicious entry changes from silent out-of-bounds write to a thrown Exception, consistent with the POV's expected NOT VULNERABLE outcome. getCanonicalPath may throw IOException, which propagates as extractFile already declares `throws Exception`.
output_json.summary: Fixed the Zip Slip path traversal (CWE-022) in org.codehaus.plexus.util.Expand.extractFile(). The method resolved attacker-controlled ZipEntry names via FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) — which follows "../" segments out of the destination via getCanonicalFile() — and then wrote/created the resulting File without verifying containment. Added a canonical-path containment check that rejects any entry resolving outside the destination directory before any write/mkdir/setLastModified occurs. A crafted entry named "../escaped.txt" now throws instead of writing outside dest.
